4.commentary: This also describes a situation that one cannot master alone. In such instances, the straight path is not the shortest. Forging ahead using only one's own strength, without the necessary preparations, would fail to secure the required support. One would realize too late that calculations were deceptive, as the circumstances relied upon prove too weak. Therefore, it is correct in this case to hold back initially and gather reliable companions upon whom one can rely to overcome the obstructions.
4.title: Six in the fourth place means:

5.text: In the midst of the greatest obstructions, Friends come.
5.commentary: Here we see the individual called to organize relief in times of distress. He must not attempt to evade obstructions, no matter how dangerously they tower before him. Because he possesses a genuinely higher calling, the power of his spirit is strong enough to attract people to his cause. They come to assist him, and he is capable of effectively organizing them, so that through the well-planned cooperation of all involved, the obstruction is overcome.
5.title: Nine in the fifth place means:

6.text: Going leads to obstructions, Coming leads to great good fortune. It is favorable to see the great man.
6.commentary: This depicts someone who has already left the world and its turmoil behind. When a time of obstruction falls upon the world, it might seem easiest for him to simply leave everything behind and escape into isolation. However, this path is closed to him. He cannot seek personal salvation alone while abandoning the world to its distress. Instead, duty calls him back once more into the world's turmoil. His very experience and inner freedom enable him to accomplish something significant and mature that brings salvation. It is therefore favorable to see the great man, in cooperation with whom the work of rescue can be fulfilled.
6.title: Six at the top means:

40.name: Deliverance
40.title: Hexagram 40 解 - Jiě / Deliverance
40.description: Richard Wilhelm's complete study and analysis of Hexagram 40 (Jiě) of the I Ching with Unicode characters and Pinyin.
40.intro: Movement sets the direction out of danger. The impediment is removed, and the difficulties are resolving. Deliverance is not yet complete; it is just beginning, and its various stages are illustrated in this hexagram.

dictamen.text: Deliverance. The southwest furthers. If there is no longer any place where one must go, returning brings good fortune. If there is still a place where one must go, speed brings good fortune.
dictamen.commentary: This refers to a time when tensions and complications begin to ease. In such times, one should return to ordinary conditions as soon as possible - this is the meaning of the southwest. These periods of transition are highly important. Just as a liberating rain releases atmospheric tension and causes all buds to burst open, a time of deliverance from an oppressive burden has a freeing and stimulating effect on life. However, one crucial point remains: triumph must not be exaggerated in such times. One should not advance further than necessary. Returning to the regular order of life as soon as deliverance is achieved brings good fortune. If any remnants still need clearing up, it should be done as quickly as possible to make a clean sweep and avoid any delays.

imagen.text: Thunder and rain arise: The image of Deliverance. Thus the superior man pardons mistakes and forgives misdeeds.
imagen.commentary: The thunderstorm has a purifying effect on the air. The superior man acts similarly toward people's mistakes and sins, which create states of tension. He brings deliverance through clarity. When transgressions come to light, he does not dwell on them; he simply passes over faults, which are unintentional errors, just as thunder dies away. He forgives misdeeds, which are intentional transgressions, just as water cleanses everything from dirt.

1.text: Without blame.
1.commentary: In keeping with the situation, few words are spoken. The obstruction is past; deliverance has arrived. One recuperates in peace and keeps still. This is precisely the right course of action after surviving difficulties.
1.title: Six at the beginning means:

2.text: One kills three foxes in the field and receives a yellow arrow. Perseverance brings good fortune.
2.commentary: The imagery is taken from the hunt. The hunter catches three crafty foxes and receives a yellow arrow as a reward. The obstructions in public life are the deceitful foxes who try to influence the ruler through flattery. They must be removed before deliverance can happen. But the battle must not be fought with improper weapons. The yellow color signifies measure and moderation in proceeding against enemies, while the arrow represents a straight direction. Dedicating oneself wholeheartedly to the task of deliverance brings an inner rectitude so powerful that it acts as a weapon against everything false and vulgar.
2.title: Nine in the second place means:

3.text: If a man carries a burden on his back and yet rides in a carriage, he thereby encourages robbers to approach. Perseverance leads to humiliation.
3.commentary:
A person has risen from poverty into a comfortable position, freed from want. If he now tries to make himself comfortable like an upstart, without his inner character suiting these easy circumstances, he attracts robbers. If he continues in this way, he will certainly bring shame upon himself.

Confucius says about this: "Carrying a burden on the back is the business of a common man. A carriage is the vehicle of a man of rank. Now, if a common man uses the vehicle of a man of rank, robbers think of taking it away from him. If a man is insolent toward those above him and harsh toward those below him, robbers think of attacking him. Careless storage invites robbers to steal. A girl's lavish adornment entices the robbery of her virtue."
3.title: Six in the third place means:

4.text: Deliver yourself from your great toe. Then the companion approaches, and you can trust him.
4.commentary: In times of stagnation, it happens that inferior people attach themselves to a superior man, and through daily habit, grow close to him and become indispensable, like the great toe to the foot, which eases walking. But when the time of deliverance approaches with its call to action, one must free oneself from such casual acquaintances with whom one does not truly belong. Otherwise, like-minded friends, whom one can actually trust and achieve things together with, will stay away out of mistrust.
4.title: Nine in the fourth place means:

5.text: If the superior man can only deliver himself, it brings good fortune. He thus proves to inferior men that he is in earnest.
5.commentary: Times of deliverance require inner resolve. Inferior people cannot be removed by prohibitions or external means. To rid oneself of them, one must first completely detach from them inwardly; they will then notice on their own that one is serious and will withdraw.
5.title: Six in the fifth place means:

6.text: The prince shoots at a hawk on a high wall. He kills it. Everything is favorable.
6.commentary:
The hawk on a high wall is the image of a powerful, inferior person in a high position who obstructs deliverance. He resists inner influences because he is hardened in his wickedness. He must be removed by force, which requires the appropriate means.

Confucius says about this: "The hawk is the object of the hunt. Bow and arrow are the tools and means. The marksman is the man who must use the means properly to achieve the purpose. The superior man hides the means within his person. He awaits the right time and then acts. How could everything fail to go well? He acts and is free. Therefore, he only needs to go forth and he captures the prey. This is how it stands with a man who acts after preparing the means."
6.title: Six at the top means:

41.name: DECREASE
41.title: Hexagram 41 損 - SǓN / DECREASE
41.description: Richard Wilhelm's comprehensive study and analysis of Hexagram 41 (SUN) of the I Ching with Unicode characters and Pinyin.
41.intro: This hexagram represents a reduction of the lower trigram to benefit the upper, as the third line-originally strong-has moved to the top, and the originally weak top line has taken its place. The lower component is thus diminished for the sake of the upper. This constitutes decrease in its purest sense. If you weaken the foundation of a building to strengthen its upper walls, the entire structure loses stability. Similarly, diminishing the wealth of the people to benefit the government is a straightforward decrease. The entire focus of the hexagram is to illustrate how this shift in wealth can occur without drying up the sources of prosperity among the people and the lower classes.

dictamen.text: Decrease combined with sincerity Brings supreme good fortune without blame. One may be perseverance in this. It is favorable to undertake something. How is this carried out? One may use two small bowls for the sacrifice.
dictamen.commentary: Decrease does not imply something negative under all circumstances. Increase and decrease come at their appointed times. The crucial point is to adapt to the time and not try to cover up poverty with empty show. When an inner truth finds expression during a time of meager resources, one should not feel ashamed of simplicity. In such times, simplicity is precisely what provides the inner strength needed to undertake new endeavors. One should not hesitate even if the outer beauty of culture, or even the elaboration of religious relationships, must suffer for the sake of simplicity. One must draw from the strength of inner conviction to compensate for the poverty of external appearances. Then the power of the content carries one past the simplicity of the form. Before God, false appearances are unnecessary. Even with modest means, the true disposition of the heart can find full expression.

imagen.text: At the foot of the mountain is the lake: the image of Decrease. Thus the superior man controls his anger and restrains his instincts.
imagen.commentary: The lake at the foot of the mountain evaporates. In doing so, it decreases to benefit the mountain, which is enriched by its moisture. The mountain represents stubborn strength that can harden into anger, while the lake represents uncontrolled joy that can develop into passionate instincts if it feeds at the expense of vital energies. Here, decrease is necessary: anger must be diminished by keeping still, and instincts must be curbed through restriction. By decreasing these lower psychological forces, the higher aspects of the soul are enriched.

1.text: When one's tasks are finished, to go quickly Is without blame. But one must consider To what extent one may decrease others.
1.commentary: It is selfless and good to place one's energy at the service of others after completing one's own urgent tasks, helping quickly where needed without making a display or boasting. However, the person in the higher position who receives this help must carefully consider how much they can accept without causing essential harm to the helpful servant or friend. Only where such sensitivity exists can one give oneself unreservedly without hesitation.
1.title: Nine at the beginning means:

2.text: Perseverance is favorable. To undertake something brings misfortune. Without decreasing oneself, One is able to increase others.
2.commentary: A noble self-awareness and consistent seriousness that compromises nothing are essential when one wishes to serve others. Someone who throws themselves away just to do the bidding of a superior diminishes their own position without bringing lasting benefit to the other. This is harmful. Serving another without giving up oneself is the only true service of lasting value.
2.title: Nine in the second place means:

3.text: When three people journey together, Their number decreases by one person. When one person journeys alone, They find their companion.
3.commentary: Where three are together, jealousy arises, and one must give way. The closest connection is only possible between two people. But when a person is lonely, they are certain to find a companion who complements them perfectly.
3.title: Six in the third place means:

4.text: If one decreases one's faults, It makes the other come quickly and bring joy. No blame.
4.commentary: Our faults often prevent even well-meaning people from approaching us. These flaws are frequently reinforced and worsened by our environment. If one can bring oneself to step down and cast them aside, it relieves well-meaning friends of an inner pressure, causing them to approach all the more quickly to mutual joy.
4.title: Six in the fourth place means:

5.text: Someone increases him indeed. Ten pairs of tortoises cannot oppose this. Supreme good fortune!
5.commentary: When someone is destined for good fortune by fate, it comes inevitably. All oracles, such as those obtained through tortoise shells, must concur in favorable signs to their advantage. They have nothing to fear, for their luck is a higher dispensation.
5.title: Six in the fifth place means:

6.text: If one is increased without decreasing others, This is without blame. Perseverance brings good fortune. It is favorable to undertake something. One obtains servants, But no longer has a private home.
6.commentary: There are people who dispense blessings to the entire world. Every increase in strength or resources granted to them benefits all people and therefore implies no decrease for others. Through persistent and diligent work, one achieves success and finds the helpers needed. Yet, what one accomplishes is not a limited private advantage; it is open and accessible to everyone.
6.title: Nine at the top means:

42.name: INCREASE
42.title: Hexagram 42 益 - Yì / INCREASE
42.description: Richard Wilhelm's comprehensive study and analysis of Hexagram 42 (Yì) of the I Ching with Unicode characters and Pinyin.
42.intro: The concept of increase is illustrated by the lowest strong line of the upper trigram moving down to place itself beneath the lower trigram. This approach reflects the fundamental principle of the Book of Changes: true ruling must be a form of service. A sacrifice made by the higher that brings about an increase for the lower is called absolute increase, highlighting the spirit that alone can truly aid the world.

dictamen.text: Increase. It is favorable to undertake something. It is favorable to cross the great water.
dictamen.commentary: When sacrifice is made from above to increase the lower, a spirit of joy and gratitude spreads among the people, which is incredibly valuable for the prosperity of the community. When people are so devoted to their leaders, great things can be accomplished, and even difficult, perilous undertakings will succeed. Therefore, in such rising times, marked by successful development, one must work and make full use of the opportunity. This period resembles the time when heaven and earth unite, when the earth shares in the creative power of heaven to form and give life to all living things. The time of increase does not last forever, so it must be utilized while it is here.

imagen.text: Wind and thunder: the image of Increase. Thus the superior person: if they see good, they imitate it; if they have faults, they rid themselves of them.
imagen.commentary: By observing how thunder and wind reinforce and increase one another, one learns the path to self-increase and self-improvement. Discovering something good in others should inspire imitation, making all goodness on earth one's own. Spotting a flaw within oneself demands that it be cast off. In doing so, one becomes free from evil. This ethical transformation represents the most vital increase of character.

1.text: It is favorable to accomplish great deeds. Supreme good fortune. No blame.
1.commentary: Experiencing great encouragement and promotion from above means you should use this newfound strength to achieve something grand, for which you otherwise might have lacked either the power or the willingness to take responsibility. By remaining free from selfishness, supreme good fortune is achieved, and by bringing about such great success, you stay free from reproach.
1.title: Nine at the beginning means:

2.text: Someone certainly increases him. Ten pairs of tortoises cannot oppose this. Constant perseverance brings good fortune. The king presents him before God. Good fortune!
2.commentary: True increase happens because you cultivate the necessary inner conditions: receptivity and a love for what is good. Consequently, what you strive for comes naturally, by a law of nature. When increase aligns so perfectly with the highest cosmic laws, no chance combination of events can block it. Everything depends on not becoming careless through unexpected luck; instead, you must make it your own through inner strength and steadfastness. Then you gain significance before God and humanity, and you can accomplish meaningful work for the benefit of the world.
2.title: Six in the second place means:

3.text: One is increased through unfortunate events. No blame if you are sincere and walk in the middle path, reporting to the prince with a seal.
3.commentary: A time of blessing and enrichment is so powerful in its effect that even otherwise unfortunate events work for the benefit of those affected. They become free from errors, and by acting in accordance with the truth, they gain such inner authority that they exert influence as if confirmed by letter and seal.
3.title: Six in the third place means:

4.text: If you walk in the middle path and report to the prince, he will follow. It is favorable to be used in moving the capital.
4.commentary: It is crucial that there are individuals who act as mediators between leaders and followers. These must be selfless personalities, especially in times of increase, when the leader's aim is to benefit the people. None of this blessing should be selfishly held back; it must truly reach those for whom it is intended. Such a mediating personality, who also exerts a positive influence on the leader, is particularly important during times of major, future-shaping undertakings that require the inner consent of all involved.
4.title: Six in the fourth place means:

5.text: If you truly have a kind heart, do not ask. Supreme good fortune! Sincerity will recognize kindness as your virtue.
5.commentary: True kindness does not calculate or question worthiness and gratitude; it flows from inner necessity. Such a truly kind heart finds its reward in being recognized, allowing its blessed influence to expand without hindrance.
5.title: Nine in the fifth place means:

6.text: He brings increase to no one. Someone may even strike him. He does not keep his heart steady. Misfortune!
6.commentary:
The meaning of the situation is that those above should increase those below through self-denial. By neglecting this duty and helping no one, you cut yourself off from the supportive influence of others and soon find yourself isolated. This invites attacks. A mindset that does not remain in harmony with the demands of the time will inevitably bring misfortune.

Confucius says regarding this line: "The superior person brings peace to his person before moving; he composes his mind before speaking; he secures his relationships before asking for something. By putting these three matters in order, the superior person is in complete safety. If one is abrupt in his movements, people will not cooperate. If one is agitated in his words, they find no echo among the people. If one asks for something without prior relationships, people will not give it. If no one stands with him, those who cause harm will approach."
6.title: Nine at the top means:

43.name: BREAKTHROUGH (RESOLUTENESS)
43.title: Hexagram 43 夬 - GUÀI / BREAKTHROUGH (RESOLUTENESS)
43.description: Richard Wilhelm's complete investigation and analysis of Hexagram 43 (GUÀI) of the I Ching with Unicode characters and Pinyin.
43.intro: This hexagram signifies a breakthrough after a long accumulation of tension, much like a swollen river bursting through its dikes, or a sudden cloudburst. Applied to human affairs, it marks a time when inferior forces are finally fading away. Their influence is on the decline, and a resolute action brings about a decisive change in circumstances. This hexagram is associated with the third month (April-May).

dictamen.text: Breakthrough. One must resolutely make the matter known at the king's court. It must be announced truthfully. Danger! One must notify one's own city. It is not beneficial to resort to arms. It is beneficial to undertake something.
dictamen.commentary:
Even if only a single inferior person holds a ruling position in a city, they can oppress the superior people. If even a single passion nests within the heart, it can cloud the reason. Passion and reason cannot coexist; therefore, an absolute struggle is necessary if the good is to prevail. However, there are specific rules for this resolute struggle to eliminate evil, and they must not be ignored if one wishes to succeed.

Resoluteness must be based on a combination of strength and friendliness.

Compromise with what is bad is impossible; it must be openly discredited under all circumstances. Likewise, one's own passions and shortcomings must not be whitewashed.

The struggle must not be conducted directly through force. Wherever evil is branded, it looks for weapons. If you do it the favor of fighting it blow for blow, you will get the short end of the stick, because you will become entangled in hatred and passion yourself. Therefore, it is essential to start with your own house: to be personally on guard against the very faults that have been condemned. In this way, the weapons of evil blunt themselves when they find no adversary. Similarly, one's own faults must not be fought directly. As long as you wrestle with them, they will always remain victorious.

The best way to fight evil is to make energetic progress in what is good.

imagen.text: The lake has risen to heaven: The image of Breakthrough. Thus the superior person dispenses wealth downward And refrains from resting on his virtue.
imagen.commentary: When the water of the lake has risen to heaven, a cloudburst is to be feared. The superior person takes this as a warning and takes timely measures to prevent a violent collapse. Anyone who wishes to hoard wealth solely for themselves, without thinking of others, will certainly experience a collapse. For all gathering is followed by scattering. Therefore, the superior person scatters while gathering. Likewise, in developing character, he is careful not to stiffen into obstinacy, but remains impressionable through continuous, strict self-examination.

1.text: Mighty in the forward-stepping toes. If one goes forward and is not equal to the task, One makes a mistake.
1.commentary: In times of resolute advancement, the very beginning is particularly difficult. One feels enthusiastic about moving forward. However, the resistance is still very strong. Therefore, it is necessary to gauge one's own strength and only engage as far as success is certain. Blind aggressiveness leads to trouble, because an unexpected setback right at the beginning can have the most disastrous consequences.
1.title: Six at the beginning means:

2.text: A cry of alarm. Arms at evening and at night. Fear nothing.
2.commentary: Readiness is everything. Resoluteness is inseparably linked with caution. If one is careful and deliberate, there is no need to be startled or agitated. By remaining vigilant at all times before danger appears, one is armed when danger approaches and has no need to fear. The superior person is on guard against what cannot yet be seen, and anxious about what cannot yet be heard; therefore, he dwells in the midst of difficulties as if they were no difficulties at all. If one develops character, people yield of their own accord. When reason triumphs, the passions withdraw on their own. Being deliberate and not forgetting one's armor is the right way to safety.
2.title: Nine in the second place means:

3.text: Being mighty in the cheekbones brings misfortune. The superior person is firmly resolved. He walks alone and falls into the rain. He gets splashed, and people murmur against him. No blame.
3.commentary: The situation one finds oneself in is ambiguous. While everyone else is engaged in a resolute struggle against the inferior element, you alone maintain a certain relationship with an inferior person. If you were to show yourself outwardly strong and turn against him before conditions are ripe, you would jeopardize the entire situation; the inferior person would then take premature counter-measures. The task of the higher person here is exceedingly difficult. He must be inwardly firmly resolved and, while interacting with the inferior person, keep himself free from any participation in his baseness. In doing so, he will naturally be misunderstood. People will think he belongs to the party of the inferior person. He is completely lonely because nobody understands him. His relationship with the inferior person defiles him in the eyes of the crowd, and people turn against him murmuring. But he bears the misunderstanding and makes no mistake, because he remains true to himself.
3.title: Nine in the third place means:

4.text: There is no skin on the thighs, And walking proves difficult. If one let oneself be led like a sheep, Remorse would disappear. But if one hears these words, One will not believe them.
4.commentary: One suffers from inner restlessness, making it impossible to remain in one's place. One wants to push forward at all costs and meets insurmountable obstacles. Thus, one is in inner conflict with one's situation. This comes from the obstinacy with which one wants to enforce one's own will. If one were to give up this obstinacy, everything would go well. But this advice, like so many good counsels, will be ignored. For obstinacy ensures that although one has ears, one does not hear.
4.title: Nine in the fourth place means:

5.text: In the face of weeds, firm resoluteness is needed. Walking in the middle remains free from blame.
5.commentary: Weeds always grow back and are difficult to eradicate. Likewise, the struggle against an inferior person in a high position requires firm resoluteness. One is in a relationship with him, and as a result, there is a fear that one might give up the struggle as hopeless. But this must not happen. One must resolutely carry on and not allow oneself to be deflected from the path. Only in this way does one remain free from blame.
5.title: Nine in the fifth place means:

6.text: No alarm call! In the end, misfortune comes.
6.commentary: Victory seems to have been won. Only a remnant of evil is left, and the time has come for its resolute eradication. Everything looks quite easy. But that is precisely where the danger lies. If one is not on guard, evil manages to escape by hiding, and once it has escaped, new misfortune arises from the remaining seeds; for evil does not die easily. One must also do a thorough job with the evil in one's own character. If one were to leave anything behind through carelessness, new trouble would grow from it.
6.title: Six at the top means:

44.name: COMING TO MEET
44.title: Hexagram 44 姤 - GÒU / COMING TO MEET
44.description: Richard Wilhelm's complete investigation and analysis of Hexagram 44 (GÒU) of the I Ching with Unicode characters and Pinyin.
44.intro: The hexagram indicates a situation where the dark principle secretly and unexpectedly forces its way back in from within and below, after having been eliminated. The feminine comes to meet the masculine of its own accord. This is a dangerous and unfavorable situation because of the possible consequences, which must be recognized in time and thus prevented. The hexagram is associated with the fifth month (June-July), because with the summer solstice, the dark principle gradually begins to rise again.

dictamen.text: Coming to Meet. The maiden is powerful. One should not marry such a maiden.
dictamen.commentary:
The rise of the inferior is depicted under the image of a bold girl who gives herself up lightly and thereby seizes power. This would not be possible if the strong and light element did not also come to meet it halfway. The inferior element looks so harmless and flattering that one finds pleasure in it. It appears so small and weak that one thinks one can jest with it without worry.

Thus, the inferior person rises only because the superior person considers them harmless and grants them power. If one were to oppose them from the very beginning, they could never gain influence.

But the time of Coming to Meet also has another side that is worth noting. While the coming to meet of the weak toward the strong must not be the rule, it has great significance at times. When heaven and earth come to meet each other, all creatures prosper. When prince and helper come to meet each other, the world is set in order. A mutual coming to meet of principles designed for each other and dependent upon each other is necessary. It must only be free from impure ulterior motives; otherwise, it leads to evil.

imagen.text: Under heaven is the wind: the image of Coming to Meet. Thus does the prince act when spreading his commands and proclaiming them to the four quarters of heaven.
imagen.commentary: The situation is similar to Hexagram 20 (Contemplation). There, the wind blows over the earth; here, it blows under heaven. In both cases, it goes everywhere. But while there, the wind on the earth below provided the image of the ruler gathering knowledge of conditions, here the wind blows from above; this indicates the influence the ruler exerts through his commands. Heaven is far from earthly things, but it sets them in motion through the wind. The ruler is far from the people, but he sets them in motion through his commands and expressions of will.

1.text: It must be checked with a brake of bronze. Perseverance brings good fortune. If one lets it take its course, one experiences misfortune. Even a lean pig has it in its nature to rage about.
1.commentary: If an inferior element has crept in, it must be checked immediately and energetically. By consistently checking it, evil consequences can be avoided. If it is allowed to take its course, misfortune will certainly result. One must not be led to take it too lightly due to the insignificance of what creeps in. As long as a pig is still young and lean, it cannot rage about much, but once it has eaten its fill and grown strong, its true nature asserts itself if it has not been restricted beforehand.
1.title: Six at the beginning means:

2.text: There is a fish in the tank. No blame! Not favorable for guests.
2.commentary: The lower element is not forced, but kept under gentle control. Then nothing bad is to be feared. However, one must ensure that it does not come into contact with outsiders, because if left loose, it would unfold its negative traits without restraint.
2.title: Nine in the second place means:

3.text: There is no skin on the thighs, and walking becomes difficult. If one is mindful of the danger, one makes no great mistake.
3.commentary: One is inwardly tempted to entangle oneself with the negative element that offers itself. This is a very dangerous situation. Fortunately, one is hindered by circumstances. One would like to, but cannot. This results in a painful indecisiveness of action. But if one realizes the danger of the situation, one will at least avoid major mistakes.
3.title: Nine in the third place means:

4.text: There is no fish in the tank. This gives rise to misfortune.
4.commentary: The lowly people must be tolerated so that they remain well-disposed. Then they can also be utilized when needed. If one becomes estranged from them and does not meet them halfway, they turn away, and they are not available when needed. One then has only oneself to blame.
4.title: Nine in the fourth place means:

5.text: A melon covered with willow leaves: hidden lines. Then it falls to one from heaven.
5.commentary: The melon, like the fish, is a symbol of the dark principle. It is sweet but rots easily, which is why it is protectively covered with willow leaves. The situation is such that a strong, high, and self-contained person protectively shields the lowly who are under his hand. He possesses the firm lines of order and beauty within himself, but he does not display them. He does not burden them with external appearances or troublesome reminders, but leaves them completely free, with firm trust in the inner transforming power inherent in a strong and pure personality. And lo and behold! Fate is favorable. The lowly are influenced and fall to him like ripe fruit.
5.title: Nine in the fifth place means:

6.text: He comes to meet with his horns. Humiliation. No blame.
6.commentary: When one has withdrawn from the world, the turmoil of the world often becomes unbearable. There are often people who, in noble pride, keep themselves distant from everything vulgar and abruptly reject it whenever it approaches them. Such people are criticized as proud and inaccessible, but since they are no longer bound to the world by duties of action, this is not serious. They know how to bear the dislike of the masses with composure.
6.title: Nine at the top means:

45.name: GATHERING TOGETHER
45.title: Hexagram 45 萃 - CUÌ / GATHERING TOGETHER
45.description: Richard Wilhelm's complete study and analysis of Hexagram 45 (CUÌ) of the I Ching with Unicode characters and Pinyin.
45.intro: This hexagram is closely related in both form and meaning to Bi, Holding Together (No. 8). While Bi features water over the earth, here we find a lake over the earth. Because a lake is a natural gathering point for water, the concept of gathering is expressed even more powerfully here. This core idea is also evident structurally: here, two strong lines in the fourth and fifth positions bring about the gathering, whereas in the eighth hexagram, only a single strong line stands in the fifth position among the weak ones.

dictamen.text: Gathering Together. Success. The king approaches his temple. It is furtherance to see the great man. This brings success. Perseverance furthers. To bring great offerings creates good fortune. It is furtherance to undertake something.
dictamen.commentary:
The gathering of people into larger communities is either natural, as seen within the family, or artificial, as seen within the state. The family gathers around the father as its head. This gathering is extended and sustained through ancestral sacrifices, where the entire clan comes together. Through the collective devotion of the living, the spirit of the ancestors becomes concentrated, preventing it from scattering and dissolving.

To gather humanity together, powerful religious forces are essential. However, a human leader must also serve as the central axis of this gathering. To unite others, this central figure must first be innerly centered and collected. Only through gathered moral strength can the world be brought into harmony. Such grand eras of unification inevitably leave great works behind, which is the deeper meaning of offering great sacrifices. Even in the secular realm, times of gathering demand the undertaking of great achievements.

imagen.text: The lake is above the earth: The image of Gathering Together. Thus the superior man renews his weapons To meet the unforeseen.
imagen.commentary: When water accumulates in a lake until it rises high above the earth, there is a constant threat of a breach. Precautions must be taken. Similarly, when people gather in large numbers, conflict easily arises; where wealth accumulates, theft easily occurs. Therefore, during times of gathering, one must prepare and arm oneself early to ward off unexpected dangers. Most human suffering comes from unexpected events for which one is unprepared. If one is ready, misfortune can be prevented.

1.text: If you are sincere, but not to the end, There will be now confusion, now gathering. If you call out, After one grasp of the hand you can laugh again. Regret nothing. Going forward is without blame.
1.commentary: The situation here involves someone who wishes to gather around a leader they look up to. However, they find themselves surrounded by a large crowd whose influence causes them to waver in their resolve. As a result, they lack a firm center for their allegiance. If they express this distress and call for help, a single gesture or grasp from the leader is enough to dispel all trouble. One must not allow themselves to be led astray. Aligning with that leader is entirely the right course of action.
1.title: Six at the beginning means:

2.text: Allowing oneself to be drawn brings good fortune and remains without blame. If one is sincere, It is also furtherance to bring a small offering.
2.commentary: During times of gathering, one should not choose their path arbitrarily. Secret, subtle forces are at work, bringing together people who naturally belong together. One must yield to this natural attraction, and no mistake will be made. Where genuine inner connections exist, grand preparations and formal rules are unnecessary. People understand each other immediately, just as the divine forces graciously accept even a small offering when it comes directly from the heart.
2.title: Six in the second place means:

3.text: Gathering together amid sighs. Nothing that furthers. Going forward is without blame. Slight humiliation.
3.commentary: One often feels a strong need to join a group, but everyone else in the vicinity has already formed close bonds, leaving one isolated. The entire situation proves to be untenable. In such a case, one must choose progress and resolutely align with a person who stands closer to the center of the gathering, someone who can introduce them into the closed circle. This is not a mistake, even if it initially places one in the somewhat humiliating position of an outsider.
3.title: Six in the third place means:

4.text: Great good fortune! No blame.
4.commentary: This line describes a person who gathers people together on behalf of their ruler. Because they do not seek personal advantage but instead work selflessly for the common unity, their efforts are crowned with success, and everything turns out right.
4.title: Nine in the fourth place means:

5.text: If one has the position that gathers, That brings no blame. If some are not yet sincerely joined, Sublime and enduring perseverance is needed, Then remorse disappears.
5.commentary: When people naturally gather around someone without that person seeking it out, it is an excellent thing. It grants a certain influence that can be thoroughly useful. However, this also introduces the possibility that some will gather around not out of genuine inner trust, but simply because of the influential position. This is certainly regrettable. The only remedy against such opportunistic people is to win their trust through increased, unswerving devotion to duty and constancy. Through this, secret mistrust is gradually overcome, and any cause for regret disappears.
5.title: Nine in the fifth place means:

6.text: Lamenting and sighing, floods of tears. No blame.
6.commentary: It can happen that one genuinely wishes to join the community but their good intentions are misunderstood. This brings sadness and lamentation. Yet, this is the right path. For through this expression of grief, the other party may come to a point of self-reflection, allowing the seeker to finally achieve the connection they so painfully missed.
6.title: Six at the top means:

46.name: PUSHING UPWARD
46.title: Hexagram 46 升 - SHENG / PUSHING UPWARD
46.description: Richard Wilhelm's complete study and analysis of Hexagram 46 (SHENG) of the I Ching with Unicode characters and Pinyin.
46.intro: The lower trigram, Xun, represents wood, while the upper, Kun, represents the earth. This implies the concept of wood growing upward out of the earth. In contrast to "Progress" (No. 35), this "Pushing Upward" requires effort, much like a plant needs strength to break through the soil. Therefore, even though this hexagram is associated with success, it is directly linked to the effort of the will. While "Progress" indicates expansion, "Pushing Upward" represents a straight, vertical ascent to power and influence, rising from obscurity and low station.

dictamen.text: Pushing Upward has supreme success. One must see the great man. Fear not! Setting forth toward the south brings good fortune.
dictamen.commentary: The upward advancement of capable elements encounters no obstacles, which is why it is accompanied by great success. The qualities that enable this rise are not violent, but rather modest and adaptable. Borne along by the favor of the times, progress is steady. One must take the initiative to seek out influential people. There is no need to fear doing so, for success will not fail to materialize. However, one must get to work; action (the underlying meaning of the south) brings good fortune.

imagen.text: Wood grows within the earth: The image of Pushing Upward. Thus the superior man, devoted in character, Heaps up small things to achieve heights and greatness.
imagen.commentary: Wood grows within the earth without haste and without rest, adapting and bending around obstacles as it reaches toward the heights. Similarly, the superior man is devoted in character and never pauses in his progress.

1.text: Pushing upward that meets with confidence brings great good fortune.
1.commentary: This represents the initial stage of ascent. Just as wood draws the strength for its growth from the root, which is located at the very bottom, the power to rise originates from this low position. It is a humble and unrecognized state. However, a deep spiritual affinity exists with the rulers above, and this shared ground creates the trust needed to achieve meaningful results.
1.title: Six at the beginning means:

2.text: If one is sincere, It is rewarding to offer even a small sacrifice. No blame.
2.commentary: A strong, capable person is assumed here. He might not fit perfectly into his surroundings, as he is somewhat unpolished and cares little for external forms. However, because he is inwardly genuine, he meets with a welcoming response, and his lack of outward formality causes no harm. Sincerity here is the natural expression of solid, inner qualities, whereas in the corresponding line of the previous hexagram, it was the result of inner humility.
2.title: Nine in the second place means:

3.text: One pushes upward into an empty city.
3.commentary: Here, all the standard obstacles to advancement vanish. Progress proceeds with remarkable ease. One follows this path without hesitation to take full advantage of the success. Outwardly, everything appears to be in perfect order. Yet, no explicitly fortunate expression is added to the text. It raises the question of how long such unobstructed success can last. Nevertheless, one should not dwell on these anxieties, as they would only paralyze one's energy; instead, one must quickly capitalize on the favor of the moment.
3.title: Nine in the third place means:

4.text: The king offers him expression at Mount Qi. Good fortune. No blame.
4.commentary: Mount Qi is located in western China, the homeland of King Wen, whose son, the Duke of Zhou, authored the text for the individual lines. This line recalls the rise of the Zhou dynasty. At that time, King Wen presented his great helpers to the god of his native mountain, granting them a place beside the ruler in the ancestral halls. This marks a stage where the upward ascent reaches its goal. One achieves renown before both humans and spiritual forces, becoming part of the circle of people who shape the nation's spiritual life, thereby gaining lasting, timeless significance.
4.title: Six in the fourth place means:

5.text: Perseverance brings good fortune. One pushes upward by steps.
5.commentary: When making steady progress, it is crucial not to become intoxicated by success. Precisely during moments of great advancement, one must remain consistently sober and avoid skipping steps. Instead, progress should be deliberate, moving forward step by step. Only this calm, steady advancement, which forces nothing, leads to the goal.
5.title: Six in the fifth place means:

6.text: Pushing upward in the dark. It is rewarding to be unremittingly persevering.
6.commentary: Anyone who blindly presses upward is inwardly deluded. Such a person only knows how to advance, never how to retreat, eventually leading to total exhaustion. In such a situation, it is critical to remain mindfully aware that one must stay conscientious and consistent. Only through this awareness does one break free from the blind impulse that always leads to misfortune.
6.title: Six at the top means:

47.name: OPPRESSION (EXHAUSTION)
47.title: Hexagram 47 困 - KÙN / OPPRESSION (EXHAUSTION)
47.description: Richard Wilhelm's complete study and analysis of Hexagram 47 (KÙN) of the I Ching with Unicode characters and Pinyin.
47.intro: The lake is above, and the water is below. This indicates that the lake is empty and dried up, conveying the core idea of exhaustion. The concept of oppression is also revealed through the structure of the lines: at the top, a dark, yielding line holds down two bright, strong lines below; at the bottom, a bright line is trapped between two dark ones. The upper trigram belongs to the dark principle, while the lower belongs to the light principle. Thus, everywhere we look, superior individuals are oppressed and restricted by the inferior.

dictamen.text: Oppression. Success. Perseverance. The great man brings good fortune. No blame. When one has something to say, it is not believed.
dictamen.commentary: Times of adversity are the exact opposite of success. Yet, they can lead to success if they encounter the right person. When a strong person faces adversity, they remain cheerful despite the danger, and this inner cheerfulness becomes the foundation for future success. This represents a stability that is stronger than fate itself. Anyone who allows their inner spirit to be broken by exhaustion will certainly fail. However, when adversity merely bends a person, it generates a counter-force within them that is bound to emerge into the light over time. No ordinary person is capable of this. Only the great man brings about good fortune and remains free of blame. Granted, his outward influence is temporarily denied to him because his words carry no weight. Therefore, in times of adversity, it is essential to be strong within and use few words.

imagen.text: There is no water in the lake: the image of Exhaustion. Thus the superior man stakes his life on following his will.
imagen.commentary: When water drains away from a lake, the lake must dry up and become exhausted. This is its fate, and it mirrors the adverse circumstances that can occur in human life. In such times, there is nothing to do but accept one's fate and remain true to oneself. This requires tapping into the deepest layer of one's true being, for only that depth is superior to any external fate.

1.text: One sits oppressed under a bare tree and strays into a gloomy valley. For three years one sees nothing.
1.commentary: When adversity strikes, the most important thing is to be strong and overcome the hardship internally. If one is weak, the distress will overwhelm them instead. Instead of moving forward, the person remains paralyzed under a bare tree, sinking deeper into darkness and melancholy. This only makes the situation more hopeless. This attitude stems from an inner delusion that must be completely overcome.
1.title: Six at the beginning means:

2.text: One is oppressed while at meat and drink. The man with the scarlet knee-bands is coming. It is radiating to offer sacrifices. To set forth brings misfortune. No blame.
2.commentary: This describes an internal state of oppression. Outwardly, everything seems fine; there is plenty to eat and drink. Yet, one feels exhausted by the mundane routines of life, seeing no way out. Help, however, comes from above. A prince—who wore scarlet knee-bands in ancient China—is searching for capable helpers. But obstacles still remain. Therefore, it is important to meet these hidden obstacles through sacrifice and prayer. Setting forth unprepared would lead to misfortune, even if the intent is morally sound. One must overcome an adverse situation through inner patience.
2.title: Nine in the second place means:

3.text: One permits oneself to be oppressed by stone and leans on thorns and thistles. One enters his house and does not see his wife. Misfortune.
3.commentary:
This shows a person who is restless and indecisive in times of distress. First, they want to push forward, but they hit obstacles that only cause oppression if they are met blindly. Trying to run through a brick wall only makes the wall feel oppressive. Then, the person leans on things that have no stability in themselves, which proves dangerous for anyone relying on them. Finally, turning back indecisively, they retreat to their own home, only to face the further disappointment of finding their wife gone.

Confucius says of this: "If a person allows himself to be oppressed by what should not oppress him, his name will surely be disgraced. If he leans on things he cannot rely upon, his life will surely be in danger. For someone who is in disgrace and danger, the hour of death approaches; how can he then expect to see his wife?"
3.title: Six in the third place means:

4.text: He comes very quietly, oppressed in a golden carriage. Humiliation, but one brings things to an end.
4.commentary: A wealthy man sees the distress of those below him and truly wishes to help. However, instead of acting quickly and decisively where needed, he approaches the matter hesitantly and formally. As a result, he encounters obstacles. Powerful and wealthy acquaintances draw him into their social circles; he must conform and cannot easily break away. This places him in a state of great embarrassment. Yet, the distress is temporary. The natural, original strength of his character eventually corrects the mistake, and the goal is achieved.
4.title: Nine in the fourth place means:

5.text: His nose and feet are cut off. One is oppressed by the man in the purple knee-bands. Joy comes softly. It is radiating to bring offerings and gifts.
5.commentary: This describes someone who deeply cares for the well-being of the people but is oppressed from both above and below (symbolized by the severed nose and feet). No help is found among those whose duty it is to assist in the rescue work (the ministers, who wore purple knee-bands). Nevertheless, things gradually take a turn for the better. Until then, one must turn to God in deep inner stillness, praying and offering sacrifices for the good of the whole.
5.title: Nine in the fifth place means:

6.text: He is oppressed by creeping vines. He moves uncertainly and says, 'Movement brings remorse.' If one feels remorse over this and makes a start, good fortune ensues.
6.commentary: One is restricted by bonds that could actually be broken with ease. The oppression is nearing its end. Yet, the person remains hesitant, still influenced by the old state of mind, fearing that any action will bring regret. But as soon as they grasp the true situation, change their mental attitude, and form a firm resolve, they will successfully master the adversity.
6.title: Six at the top means:

48.name: THE WELL
48.title: Hexagram 48 井 - JǏNG / THE WELL
48.description: Richard Wilhelm's complete study and analysis of Hexagram 48 (JǏNG) of the I Ching with Unicode characters and Pinyin.
48.intro: Wood is below, water is above. Wood descends into the earth to bring up water. This is the image of the ancient Chinese pole-well. The wood does not refer to the buckets, which were made of clay in ancient times, but to the wooden pole used to lift the water from the well. The image also points to the plant kingdom, which lifts water from the earth through its veins. The well, from which water is drawn, further contains the idea of an inexhaustible supply of nourishment.

dictamen.text: The Well. The town may be changed, but the well cannot be changed. It neither decreases nor increases. They come and go and draw from the well. If one has almost reached the water of the well but the rope does not yet go all the way down, or if one breaks the jug, this brings misfortune.
dictamen.commentary:
Capital cities were sometimes relocated in ancient China, partly due to favorable locations and partly during changes of dynasties. The architectural style changed over the centuries, but the form of the well has remained the same from ancient times to the present day. Thus, the well is an image of the social organization of humanity in its most primitive necessities of life, which is independent of all political configurations. Political structures and nations change, but human life and its requirements remain eternally the same. This cannot be altered. This life is also inexhaustible. It becomes neither less nor more and is there for everyone. Generations come and go, and they all enjoy life in its inexhaustible abundance.

However, two things are necessary for a good state or social organization. One must go down to the very foundations of life. Any superficiality in the social order that leaves the deepest needs of life unsatisfied is just as imperfect as if no attempt at order had been made at all. Likewise, negligence that causes the jug to break is harmful. If, for example, the military protection of a state is so exaggerated that it provokes wars through which the power of the state is destroyed, this is a breaking of the jug. This hexagram also applies to the individual. However much people's talents and education may differ, human nature at its foundation is the same in everyone. And every person can draw from the inexhaustible wellspring of divine human nature during their development. But here, too, two dangers threaten: first, that one does not penetrate to the actual roots of humanity but gets stuck in convention - such a superficial education is just as bad as no education at all - or that one suddenly breaks down and neglects the cultivation of one's nature.

imagen.text: Water is above wood: the image of the Well. Thus the superior man encourages the people at their work and exhorts them to help one another.
imagen.commentary: Below is the trigram Xùn, wood; above is the trigram Kǎn, water. The wood draws the water upward. Just as wood functioning as an organism mimics the activity of the well, benefiting all parts of the plant, the superior man organizes human society so that it works together like a plant organism for the good of the whole.

1.text: The mud of the well is not drunk. No animals come to an old well.
1.commentary: If someone loiters in the swampy lowlands, their life sinks into the mud. Such a person loses their significance for humanity. Those who throw themselves away will no longer find others coming to them. In the end, no one cares about them anymore.
1.title: Six at the beginning means:

2.text: At the well-hole one shoots fishes. The jug is broken and leaks.
2.commentary:
The water itself is clear, but it is not being used. Thus, only fish live in the well, and whoever comes only comes to catch fish; but the jug is broken, so the fish cannot be kept in it.

This describes a situation where someone possesses good talents, but they are neglected. No one cares about them. As a result, they deteriorate internally. They associate with common people and can no longer accomplish anything worthwhile.
2.title: Nine in the second place means:

3.text: The well is cleaned, but no one drinks from it. This is my heart's sorrow, for one could draw from it. If the king were clear-minded, all would share in the good fortune.
3.commentary: An able person is present here. He resembles a cleaned well whose water is fit to drink. But he is not being utilized. This is the sorrow of the people who know him. The desire is for the ruler to find out about him; then it would be a stroke of good fortune for everyone involved.
3.title: Nine in the third place means:

4.text: The well is being lined with stone, no blame.
4.commentary: When a well is being lined with stone, it cannot be used for a while, but the work is not in vain; it ensures that the water remains clear. Similarly, there are times in life when one must put oneself in order. During this period, one may not be able to achieve anything for others, but it is nevertheless valuable because internal cultivation increases one's strength and abilities, allowing one to achieve much more afterward.
4.title: Six in the fourth place means:

5.text: In the well is a clear, cold spring from which one can drink.
5.commentary: This is a good well that has a spring of living water at its core. A man who possesses such virtues is born to be a savior and leader of humanity. He has the water of life. Yet, the sign of "good fortune" is missing. With a well, everything depends on the water being drawn. The best water exists only as a possibility for human refreshment as long as it is not lifted. Likewise, with leaders of humanity, everything depends on people drinking from their source and translating their words into life.
5.title: Nine in the fifth place means:

6.text: One draws from the well without hindrance. It is reliable. Supreme good fortune!
6.commentary: The well is there for everyone. No prohibition restricts those who draw from it. No matter how many come, they find what they need, for the well is reliable. It has a constant source and does not dry up; therefore, it is a great blessing for the whole land. This represents the truly great person who is inexhaustibly rich in internal virtue. The more people draw from him, the greater his wealth becomes.
6.title: Six at the top means:

49.name: REVOLUTION
49.title: Hexagram 49 革 - GE / REVOLUTION
49.description: Richard Wilhelm's complete study and analysis of Hexagram 49 (GE) of the I Ching with Unicode characters and Pinyin.
49.intro: The hexagram originally signifies an animal's pelt, which changes throughout the year through molting. From this, the word is extended to mean the molts within political life, the great revolutions associated with a change of government. The two figures composing the hexagram are the two youngest daughters, Lí and Duì, just as in Hexagram 38, Kuí (Opposition). But while in Opposition the elder of the two stands above, resulting essentially only in a conflict of tendencies, here the younger is on top, and the effects work directly against each other, the forces combating one another like fire and water (the Lake), where each strives to destroy the other. Hence the idea of revolution.

dictamen.text: Revolution. On your own day, you find belief. Supreme success, furthering through perseverance. Remorse disappears.
dictamen.commentary:
Political revolutions are matters of extreme gravity. They should only be undertaken as a last resort, when no other way out remains. Not everyone is called to lead them, but only he who possesses the confidence of the people, and even then, only when the time is ripe. One must proceed in the proper manner, causing the people to rejoice and preventing excesses through enlightenment. Furthermore, one must be entirely free from selfish goals and must truly relieve the distress of the people. Only then is there nothing to regret.

Times change, and with them their demands. Just as the seasons change in the course of the year, so too do the spring and autumn of peoples and nations occur in the cosmic year, necessitating social transformations.

imagen.text: Fire in the Lake: the image of Revolution. Thus the superior man sets the calendar in order and makes the seasons clear.
imagen.commentary: The fire below and the lake above combat and destroy each other. Similarly, throughout the year, a battle takes place between the light and the dark forces, manifesting as the revolution of the seasons. Man becomes master over the changes of nature when he recognizes their regularity and divides the course of time accordingly. This brings order and clarity into the seemingly chaotic shift of seasons, allowing one to prepare in advance for the requirements of different times.

1.text: One is wrapped in the hide of a yellow cow.
1.commentary: Changes should only be undertaken when it is no longer possible to do otherwise. Therefore, utmost restraint is necessary at first. One must become entirely firm within and practice moderation - yellow is the color of the middle, and the cow is the symbol of docility - and undertake nothing for the time being, as any premature strike brings evil consequences.
1.title: Nine at the beginning means:

2.text: On one's own day, one may radicalize. Setting forth brings good fortune. No blame.
2.commentary: When all attempts to reform conditions have been tried without success, the necessity of a revolution arises. However, such a profound upheaval must be well prepared. A man must be present who possesses the necessary capabilities and public trust. One may then turn to such a man. This brings good fortune and is not a mistake. It is initially a matter of one's inner stance toward the new order that must come. One must, as it were, go out to meet it. Only in this way is it prepared.
2.title: Six in the second place means:

3.text: Setting forth brings misfortune. Perseverance brings danger. When the talk of revolution has gone around three times, one may turn toward it, and one will find belief.
3.commentary: When change is necessary, there are two errors that must be avoided. One is too rapid and ruthless a procedure, which is associated with misfortune. The other is over-conservative hesitation, which is also dangerous. One must not listen to every voice crying out for a change of the status quo. Yet, one must not ignore repeated and well-founded complaints either. When the word of change comes to someone three times and has been thoroughly weighed, one may grant it belief and engage with it. Then one will find belief and achieve something.
3.title: Nine in the third place means:

4.text: Remorse disappears. One finds belief. Changing the state order brings good fortune.
4.commentary: Radical changes require the necessary authority. Both inner strength of character and an influential position must be present. What is done must correspond to a higher truth and must not spring from arbitrary or petty motives; then it brings great good fortune. If no such inner truth underlies a revolution, it is always an evil and will have no success. For in the end, people only support undertakings for whose inner justice they have an instinctive feeling.
4.title: Nine in the fourth place means:

5.text: The great man changes like a tiger. Even before he consults the oracle, he finds belief.
5.commentary: A tiger's pelt, with its clearly visible black stripes on a yellow background, is distinctly patterned and visible from afar. It is the same with the revolutions brought about by a great man: large, clear guidelines become visible for everyone to understand. Thus, he does not need to consult the oracle first, for the people join him quite of their own accord.
5.title: Nine in the fifth place means:

6.text: The superior man changes like a panther. The inferior man molts in the face. Setting forth brings misfortune. Remaining in perseverance brings good fortune.
6.commentary: After the major, fundamental questions are settled, minor transformations in detail and more precise executions are still necessary. These are comparable to the distinct but smaller spots of the panther's pelt. A change also occurs among the inferior people as a result. They likewise molt in accordance with the new order. Admittedly, this molting is not deep-seated, but that is not to be expected either. One must be satisfied with what is possible. To try to go too far and achieve too much would lead to unrest and misfortune. For what should be striven for through a great revolution are clear, consolidated conditions that grant a general reassurance within the limits of what is currently possible.
6.title: Six at the top means:

50.name: THE CALDRON
50.title: Hexagram 50 鼎 - DING / THE CALDRON
50.description: Richard Wilhelm's complete study and analysis of Hexagram 50 (DING) of the I Ching with Unicode characters and Pinyin.
50.intro:
The entire hexagram visually represents the image of the caldron: at the bottom are the legs, followed by the belly, then the ears or handles, and at the very top, the rings for carrying. The image of the caldron naturally suggests the idea of nourishment. Cast in bronze, the caldron was the vessel that held cooked food in the ancestral temple and at great feasts. From it, the host would ladle food into the bowls of the guests.

The Well also carries the secondary meaning of providing nourishment, but primarily for the common people. The Caldron, as a vessel of refined culture, suggests the fostering and nourishment of capable men, whose talents ultimately benefited the state government (see the four hexagrams concerning nourishment: Numbers 5, 27, 48, and 50).

This hexagram and "The Well" are the only two signs in the Book of Changes that represent concrete, man-made objects. Yet here, too, the concept has its abstract dimension. Below is Xùn, representing wood and wind; above is Lí, representing the flame. Thus, it depicts a flame kindled by wood and wind, which likewise suggests the preparation of food.

dictamen.text: The Caldron. Supreme good fortune. Success.
dictamen.commentary:
While The Well deals with the social foundation of society-which is like water nourishing the wood-this hexagram indicates the cultural superstructure of society. Here, it is the wood that serves as nourishment for the flame, representing the spiritual realm. Everything visible must ascend and extend into the invisible. Through this process, it receives its proper consecration and clarity, rooting itself firmly in the cosmic order.

Thus, culture is shown here reaching its summit in religion. The caldron is used for making sacrifices to God. The highest earthly values must be offered to the divine. However, the truly divine does not manifest apart from the human. The highest revelation of God appears through prophets and holy men. Honoring them is the true veneration of God. The will of God, revealed through them, must be accepted with humility; this brings an inner enlightenment and a true understanding of the world, leading to great good fortune and success.

imagen.text: Fire over wood: the image of the Caldron. Thus the superior man consolidates his fate by making his position correct.
imagen.commentary: Wood serves as the destiny of the fire; as long as wood is present below, the fire burns above. It is the same with human life. Within every human being lies a destiny that lends strength to their existence. If one succeeds in assigning the right place to life and fate, one consolidates that destiny, bringing life into immediate harmony with it. These words contain hints regarding the nurturing of life, passed down from mouth to mouth through the secret teachings of Chinese yoga practice.

1.text: A caldron with upturned legs. Furthering to remove stagnating matter. One takes a concubine for the sake of her son. No blame.
1.commentary:
Turning a caldron upside down before using it is of no negative consequence; on the contrary, this is how accumulated refuse is cleared out. A concubine holds a low social standing, but because she bears a son, she rises to a position of honor.

Both parables express the idea that in times of high culture, as indicated by this hexagram, anyone of good will can find a way to succeed. No matter how lowly a person's starting point may be, if they are willing to purify themselves, they will be accepted. They will find themselves in a position where they can achieve fruitful results and, consequently, win recognition.
1.title: Six at the beginning means:

2.text: There is food in the caldron. My comrades are envious, but they cannot harm me. Good fortune!
2.commentary: In times of high culture, everything depends on actual achievement. If a person relies solely on real accomplishments, they may encounter envy and ill will, but this presents no real danger. The more one limits oneself to positive achievements, the less envious people can do to cause harm.
2.title: Nine in the second place means:

3.text: The handle of the caldron is altered. One is impeded in his way of life. The fat of the pheasant is not eaten. Once the rain falls, remorse is spent; Good fortune comes at last.
3.commentary:
The handle is the part by which the caldron is lifted. If the handle is altered, the caldron cannot be lifted or used, and the fine food inside-like the rich fat of pheasants-regrettably serves to nourish no one.

This describes someone who, in a period of high culture, finds themselves in a position where they are ignored and unacknowledged by others. This constitutes a severe hindrance to their effectiveness. All their excellent qualities and intellectual gifts are wasted in this manner. However, one must simply ensure that they possess true spiritual wealth within. If so, the time will surely come when the obstacles dissolve and everything turns out well.

The release of tension is symbolized here, as elsewhere, by the falling of rain.
3.title: Nine in the third place means:

4.text: The caldron breaks its legs. The prince's meal is spilled, and his person is soiled. Misfortune!
4.commentary:
A person faces a heavy, highly responsible task that they are not capable of fulfilling. Moreover, because they do not devote their full energy to this task but instead associate with inferior people, the execution fails completely. In doing so, they bring shame and disgrace upon themselves.

Confucius remarked on this: "Weak character coupled with an honored position, meager knowledge paired with large plans, small strength alongside heavy responsibility-these seldom escape misfortune."
4.title: Nine in the fourth place means:

5.text: The caldron has yellow handles, golden carrying rings. Perseverance furthers.
5.commentary: This describes a person in a ruling position who is accessible and modest by nature. Through this inner attitude, they succeed in finding strong and capable helpers who complement them and assist in their work. It is essential not to let oneself be swayed from this stance, which requires continuous inner self-effacement, but to hold fast to it.
5.title: Six in the fifth place means:

6.text: The caldron has jade rings. Great good fortune! Nothing that would not be furthering.
6.commentary: In the preceding line, the carrying rings were called golden to emphasize their strength. Here they are described as being made of jade. Jade is characterized by its ability to combine hardness with a mild, gentle luster. From the standpoint of the leader who is open to counsel, this advice acts as a powerful aid. Here, the counsel is described from the standpoint of the sage who gives it. In doing so, it will be gentle and refined, like noble jade. In this way, the work finds favor in the eyes of the divine, which grants great good fortune, and becomes acceptable to people, causing everything to go well.
6.title: Nine at the top means:

51.name: THE AROUSING
51.title: Hexagram 51 震 - ZHÈN / THE AROUSING
51.description: Richard Wilhelm's complete study and analysis of Hexagram 51 (ZHÈN) of the I Ching with Unicode characters and Pinyin.
51.intro: The hexagram Zhèn represents the eldest son, who seizes rule with energy and power. A Yang line develops below two Yin lines and presses upward forcefully. This movement is so vehement that it causes terror. It is symbolized by thunder, which bursts forth from the earth, causing fear and trembling through its shock.

dictamen.text: The Arousing brings success. Thunder comes: oh, oh! Laughing words: ha, ha! The shock terrifies for a hundred miles, and he does not let the sacrificial spoon and chalice fall.
dictamen.commentary: The shock rising from the manifestation of God within the earth fills man with fear, but this fear of God is a good thing, for it allows happiness and joy to follow. When someone has learned internally what fear and trembling mean, they are protected against terror from external influences. Even when thunder roars, terrifying everything within a radius of a hundred miles, one remains so composed and reverent internally that the sacrificial ritual is not interrupted. Such a deep, inner seriousness, which causes all external terrors to bounce off harmlessly, is the frame of mind that leaders and rulers of men must possess.

imagen.text: Continuous thunder: the image of the Arousing. Thus the superior man, in fear and trembling, sets his life in order and examines himself.
imagen.commentary: The continuous thunder carries fear and trembling with its shock. Thus, the superior man always stands in reverence before the manifestation of God, putting his life in order and searching his heart to see if anything secretly contradicts the divine will. In this way, reverence becomes the foundation of true character building.

1.text: Thunder comes: oh, oh! Afterward follow laughing words: ha, ha! Good fortune!
1.commentary: The fear and trembling of the shock come upon a person first, making them feel at a disadvantage compared to others. But this is only temporary. Once you pass through the judgment, relief follows. Thus, the very terror you must initially face ultimately brings good fortune.
1.title: Nine at the beginning means:

2.text: The shock comes with danger. A hundred-thousand fold you lose your treasures and must climb the nine hills. Do not chase after them. After seven days you will get them back.
2.commentary: This describes a situation where a shock brings danger and severe losses. Circumstances are such that resisting the direction of the times is futile and will yield no success. Therefore, one should simply retreat to high areas that remain inaccessible to the threatening dangers. One must accept the loss of property and not worry excessively about it. Without chasing after these possessions, they will return on their own once the period of unsettling shocks has passed.
2.title: Six in the second place means:

3.text: The shock comes and makes one bewildered. If one acts as a result of the shock, one remains free from misfortune.
3.commentary:
There are three kinds of shock: the shock of heaven, which is thunder; the shock of fate; and finally, the shock of the heart.

Here, it is less about inner shock and more about the shock of fate. During such turbulent times, it is all too easy to lose one's presence of mind, misjudging every opportunity for action and mutely letting fate take its course. If you allow the shock of fate to spur you into inner movement, you will overcome these external blows without much difficulty.
3.title: Six in the third place means:

4.text: The shock sinks into the mud.
4.commentary: The success of inner movement depends partly on circumstances. If the environment offers neither resistance to fight energetically nor yielding compliance to achieve victory, but is instead as sticky and sluggish as mud, the movement becomes paralyzed.
4.title: Nine in the fourth place means:

5.text: The shock goes to and fro: danger. Yet one loses nothing at all, only there is business to attend to.
5.commentary: This does not describe a single shock, but a repeated one that leaves no time to catch one's breath. Nevertheless, the shock brings no loss, because one is careful to stay at the center of the movement, thus escaping the fate of being tossed helplessly back and forth.
5.title: Six in the fifth place means:

6.text: The shock brings ruin and anxious looking around. Going ahead brings misfortune. If it has not yet reached one's own body, but has only reached the neighbor, there is no blame. One's companions have talk to make.
6.commentary:
When inner shock reaches its peak, it robs a person of presence of mind and clarity of vision. In such a state of agitation, it is naturally impossible to act prudently. The right course of action is to keep still until composure and clarity return.

However, one can only do this as long as they haven't caught the panic themselves, even if the disastrous effects of this excitement can already be observed in the surroundings. By withdrawing from action in time, one remains free from error and harm. Yet, companions in their state of excitement, who refuse to be warned, will certainly be dissatisfied. But one must not pay any attention to that.
6.title: Six at the top means:

52.name: KEEPING STILL
52.title: Hexagram 52 艮 - GÈN / KEEPING STILL
52.description: Richard Wilhelm's complete study and analysis of Hexagram 52 (GÈN) of the I Ching with Unicode characters and Pinyin.
52.intro:
The image of the hexagram is the mountain, the youngest son of heaven and earth. The masculine principle is at the top, where it naturally strives to be, while the feminine principle is below, where the direction of its movement leads. This brings about rest, as the movement has reached its normal conclusion.

Applied to human affairs, the hexagram addresses the challenge of achieving peace of heart. The heart is exceedingly difficult to bring to rest. While Buddhism seeks stillness by fading out all movement into Nirvana, the Book of Changes holds the view that rest is merely a polar state that constantly finds its complement in movement.

Perhaps the words of the text contain instructions for the practice of yoga.

dictamen.text: Keeping still of his back, so that he no longer feels his body. He goes into his courtyard and does not see his people. No blame.
dictamen.commentary:
True quiet means keeping still when the time has come to keep still, and going forward when the time has come to go forward. In this way, rest and movement are in harmony with the demands of the time, bringing forth the light of life.

The hexagram represents the end and the beginning of all movement. The back is named because it holds all the nerve pathways that mediate movement. When the movement of these spinal nerves is brought to a standstill, the ego with its restlessness vanishes, so to speak. When a person has become inwardly quiet, they can turn toward the outside world. They no longer see the conflict and turmoil of individual beings within it, thereby gaining the true peace necessary to understand the great laws of world events and act accordingly. Whoever acts from this depth makes no mistake.

imagen.text: Mountains standing close together: the image of Keeping Still. Thus the superior man does not permit his thoughts to go beyond his situation.
imagen.commentary: The heart thinks constantly; this cannot be changed. However, the movements of the heart, meaning its thoughts, should restrict themselves to the present situation of life. Any thinking beyond this only causes the heart to grow weary and sore.

1.text: Keeping still of his toes. No blame. Continued perseverance furthers.
1.commentary: Keeping the toes quiet means stopping before one has even begun to move. The beginning is a time when few mistakes are made. One is still in harmony with original innocence. Things are perceived intuitively as they are, remaining uninfluenced by the clouding effects of personal interests and desires.
